subquestions.text_open: 2-1-2 Calculate the conditional reduction potential of $\mathrm{Fe(CN)_6^{3-}}$ to $\mathrm{Fe(CN)_6^{4-}}$ in $\mathrm{mol}\cdot\mathrm{L}^{-1}$ HCl. Given $\varphi^\Theta_{\mathrm{Fe(CN)_6^{3-}/Fe(CN)_6^{4-}}}=0.36\ \mathrm{V}$; $\mathrm{H_3Fe(CN)_6}$ is a strong acid; $\mathrm{H_4Fe(CN)_6}$ has $\mathrm{p}K_{\mathrm{a3}}=2.2$ and $\mathrm{p}K_{\mathrm{a4}}=4.2$; neglect ionic effects.

2-2 Dissolve a 1.000 g sample containing sodium iodate and sodium periodate in a 250 mL volumetric flask and dilute to the mark. Transfer 50.00 mL to an Erlenmeyer flask, adjust to weakly basic pH, add excess potassium iodide, and titrate with 0.04000 mol·L^{-1} sodium thiosulfate; 10.00 mL is consumed. Transfer another 20.00 mL, acidify with hydrochloric acid, add excess potassium iodide, and titrate with sodium thiosulfate of the same concentration; 30.00 mL is consumed. 2-2-1 What reaction occurs in the first titration? Write its ionic equation and explain why the solution must be adjusted to weakly basic conditions.
2-2-2 Calculate the mass percentages of sodium iodate and sodium periodate.

2-2-3 In theory, this method can measure the mass percentages of sodium iodate and sodium periodate fairly accurately. In a student laboratory, however, it is difficult to obtain an accurate result, defined as an error within 0.1%. Explain the principal reason in terms of experimental readings. (No more than 20 words.)
